nodes.name: Webhook: /instagram-post
nodes.notes: Must match N8N_INSTAGRAM_WEBHOOK_URL on the AURON side exactly -- default is http://n8n:5678/webhook/instagram-post, so this node's path must be 'instagram-post'. AURON calls this ONLY after a human has explicitly approved the candidate (see instagram_content/service.py publish()) -- nothing upstream of this webhook makes that decision.

nodes.name: Is Reel?
nodes.notes: Checked before the single_image filter -- a reel request takes the kept output into the reel chain below; everything else (single_image, unsupported carousel) falls through (discarded output) into the existing single_image filter untouched.

nodes.name: Google Drive: Make Video Viewable by Link
nodes.notes: Same reasoning as the image path's public-link step -- Instagram's own reel-container step fetches the video itself from a URL, AURON never uploads bytes. Note: Drive's uc?export=view link can serve an HTML 'can't scan this file for viruses' interstitial instead of raw bytes for very large files -- not handled here; if reel container creation starts failing with an HTML body instead of a real API error, that's the likely cause.

nodes.name: Instagram: Create Reel Media Container
nodes.notes: media_type=REELS tells Instagram this container is a Reel, not a feed video -- Instagram fetches the video itself from video_url by reference, same as the image path. A reel container takes materially longer to process than an image one, which is why this path polls status_code below instead of the fixed wait the single_image path still uses (separate, not touched here).

nodes.name: Wait for Reel Processing
nodes.notes: Loop target: re-entered on every 'not finished yet' pass below until status_code is FINISHED or the hard cap of 20 attempts is hit.

nodes.name: Reel Polling Exhausted?
nodes.notes: $runIndex is THIS node's own execution count within the current run -- it increments every time the loop cycles back through 'Wait for Reel Processing' and reaches this node again. 0-indexed, so runIndex 19 is the 20th pass: 20 attempts x 5s wait = up to ~100s of polling before giving up with a clear timeout error instead of looping forever.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ { "error": "Reel container did not reach FINISHED after 20 status checks (~100s) -- Instagram is still processing it or something went wrong. Not published." } }}

nodes.name: Only single_image (for tonight)
nodes.notes: reel requests never reach this node -- they're routed by 'Is Reel?' above before this filter runs. This filter now only distinguishes single_image from carousel (still unsupported): carousel needs a second container-per-item + parent-container step, a real but separate addition, not yet wired here. Anything that isn't single_image falls through to 'Unsupported format -> error response' below rather than silently mishandling it.

nodes.name: Google Drive: Make File Viewable by Link
nodes.notes: Instagram's own media-container step cURLs the image itself -- it must be reachable at a public URL at the moment of the request, AURON never uploads bytes directly. Setting 'anyone with the link, reader' is the minimum needed; the file is NOT indexed or discoverable, only fetchable by anyone who has this exact URL, which only this workflow ever sees.

nodes.name: Instagram: Create Media Container
nodes.notes: AURON_IG_USER_ID and AURON_IG_ACCESS_TOKEN are set via n8n's own built-in Variables screen (left sidebar -> Overview -> Variables tab, or Settings -> Variables depending on version) -- NOT Docker environment variables, so no container restart or docker-compose edit is needed to change them. NEVER hardcoded here, NEVER committed to this JSON file. The access token is the long-lived Instagram User token from the Business Login for Instagram flow (graph.instagram.com host -- NOT graph.facebook.com, which rejects this token type with 'Invalid OAuth access token').

nodes.name: Wait for Instagram to Process
nodes.notes: A fixed wait is a reasonable v1 for a single image (usually processes in a few seconds) -- the more correct version polls GET /{container-id}?fields=status_code until it reports FINISHED rather than assuming. Worth upgrading before this handles video/reels, where processing can take much longer and a fixed wait would be unreliable.

nodes.name: Respond: media_id
nodes.notes: AURON's publisher.py reads exactly this field -- 'media_id' -- from the response body. Anything else, or a non-2xx status, is treated as a failed publish (item.status becomes post_failed, a notification goes out) rather than silently assumed successful.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ { "error": "post_format " + $json.body.post_format + " is not yet wired in this n8n workflow -- only single_image is live tonight." } }}

nodes.name: Unsupported format -> error response
nodes.notes: A clear, honest 422 rather than a silent no-op or a misleading success -- AURON's own publisher.py treats any non-2xx as a real failure and notifies Brano, which is exactly the right behavior here rather than a post that looks approved but never actually went out.
